why: hq_backup_snapshot copies public tables and auth accounts only; its own header and the restore doc say Storage files are left out on purpose, and nothing in deploy/ or scripts/ copies Storage

Copies live only in the HQ Worker's KV (wrangler.jsonc:91) with a 7-day expiry (backup.js KEEP_SECONDS); no second store anywhere. But the data it protects lives in Supabase, a different provider, so losing the Cloudflare account loses the backups, not the data; and 7 days is the promise in the privacy page, chosen on purpose

gym_page_reports is written by gym_page_report_send but no HQ, Worker or migration ever reads it (grep finds no reader), and hq_hide_gym_page has no caller in deploy/hq. Part overstated: HQ does have a per-gym 'Switch the web page off' button (0090, apps/hq/public/logic.js:925-934) that stops the page opening, so a page can be taken down once someone hears of it

HQ's manual confirm calls apply_gym_payment, which keeps plan Pro and writes a gym_plan_changes row (0063:259-282); the only thing that applies it is hq_billing_daily, called only by runBillingDaily, which returns 'not set up' unless var BILLING is 'test' with keys (billing.js:62,412); wrangler.jsonc sets no BILLING var

The HQ delete-gym route runs hq_delete_gym and removes Storage files only (api.js:575-592); no code anywhere deletes pay_connections or pay_requests rows (grep of DELETE FROM in deploy/ finds none), and wipeSpentKeys only blanks keys after a desk Disconnect (pay.js:1009-1016), against the 30-day promise in data-agreement.html:58

flushPending drops the kept push only on STALE (cloud.ts:1050-1053); a FINAL_REFUSAL (OWNER_ONLY, SUSPENDED, plan refusals, cloud.ts:432) is rethrown with pending kept, so every later action re-sends it first (1162) and the poll swallows the error (920-925), while pushOnce treats the same refusals as final (1076-1081). Needs a no-answer save followed by a status change, and a page reload clears the in-memory push

A failed phoneContents() becomes zeros (BackupFilePanels.tsx:211), so hasData is false (298) and onReplace restores at once with no question (265-269); the Drive path does ask but a failed count reads as 0 removed (BackupCard.tsx:258-264). Softened: the file restore still offers Undo afterwards (setUndo(r.undo), line 252) except on the welcome screen, and the count failing while the restore succeeds is rare
